title: Check and decrement an async-stored amount in one per-owner critical section

facts.note: Bun stack; code may also run on Node.
Use cases and store adapters, derived from path.
Test files are evidence, not targets.
Task text mentions consuming a limited amount.

Applies to any path that reads an amount from an async store, decides on it and writes a decremented value for the same key, whether in one function or composed across functions/adapter methods, and whether or not further awaits sit between read and write. Detection limitation (separate from applicability): a first observer can reliably find only intra-function read→write pairs; cross-function composition needs call-graph analysis or LLM judgement.
Whether the diff touches the check-and-decrement path.

fires: A use case awaits `store.get(accountId)`, checks `balance >= amount`, awaits a price lookup, then awaits `store.set(accountId, balance - amount)` with no lock or conditional write.
A use case awaits `store.get(id)`, checks, then immediately awaits `store.set(id, stock - n)` with no other await in between.
A store adapter exposes separate `read` and `write` methods and a use case (or a helper it calls) composes them to decrement inventory stock.
A quota-consumption endpoint re-validates availability before acquiring a lock but not inside it.
doesNotFire: Read-only checks that never decrement (previews, quotes, balance display).
Pure domain functions that compute a new balance without touching a store.

given: Application or store-adapter code reads an amount (balance, stock, quota) from an async store, decides on it, then decrements it — in one function or across composed calls.
when: The read–decide–decrement path is written or changed.
then: Make the check and the decrement one critical section per owner key (per-key serialisation or an atomic conditional write), so concurrent requests can never spend the same units.
prefer: Per-owner async mutex/queue: `await locks.run(ownerId, async () => { read; check; write })`.
Or a store conditional write (expected version / compare-and-set) with retry on conflict (e.g. a capped retry loop).
Re-check every precondition (status, ownership, idempotency key, available amount) inside the section.
Run debit-independent fallible steps (pricing, tax/config lookup, validation) before the debit; if a later step fails, undo the debit before returning the error.
Persist the debit and its result record together, or in a compensable order.
avoid: Separate awaited read and write outside one section: each `await` is a race window, even single-threaded.
A global lock across unrelated owners when a per-owner one suffices.
Checking only before acquiring the lock.
unless: The store already performs check and decrement as one atomic operation (e.g. a single conditional update rejecting insufficient amounts); no extra lock is needed.
why: Interleaved awaits let two requests read the same amount and both spend it, overspending or going negative; a debit without its record silently loses units.
evidence: A concurrency test fires parallel requests (`Promise.all`) for one owner against the async store: total debited ≤ available, balance never negative, sum applied == sum removed.
A test where a step after the debit fails leaves the balance unchanged, with any debit compensated so no units are debited without a recorded result.
Reviewer sees the precondition checks and the decrement inside the same lock callback or conditional write.
verifier_detail: Flag any path where an awaited read of an amount and the write of the decremented value for the same key are not enclosed in one per-key lock/queue call and not replaced by a conditional write (version/CAS/`WHERE amount >= n`) — regardless of whether other awaits sit between them, and including read/write composed across helper functions or adapter methods (follow calls or use reviewer judgement where static detection cannot).

Flag a lock keyed by a constant (global) that serialises operations across unrelated owners only when per-owner serialisation would suffice, i.e. the critical section reads and writes state of a single owner key only; do not flag a global lock when the section legitimately spans multiple owners or shared state (e.g. a transfer between two accounts or a shared pool), where reviewer judgement decides.
Flag precondition checks (status, ownership, idempotency key, available amount) that appear only before lock acquisition and are not repeated inside.
Flag fallible calls after the debit with no compensating credit on their error path; flag fallible debit-independent steps (pricing, tax/config lookup, validation) placed after the debit.
Flag debit and result record persisted in separate non-compensated writes.

Concurrency test must issue genuinely concurrent requests (Promise.all or equivalent) — enough that their combined demand exceeds the available amount so contention is exercised — against an async (not synchronous in-memory) store; sequential loops do not count.
audit: Written for PLT-85 as a new general convention; no canonical source. Derived from spec.md.
splitSuggestion: Compensate or pre-order fallible steps around a debit (failure after debit leaves no units debited without a recorded result) could become its own rule; kept here as prefer/evidence.
Persist a debit and its result record atomically could become its own rule; kept here as prefer.
